items.a: A platform to build, deploy and govern AI solutions: agents, workflows, knowledge bases and interfaces. You describe the problem and the Composer builds the solution; then you publish it with environments, versions, traces and cost control.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: Not to get started: the Composer and the Studio cover day-to-day work from the interface. If you code, everything is versioned Python you can edit, run locally with the CLI or sync with GitHub.

In European Union regions. In strict residency mode, models are used only through AWS Bedrock in the EU and embeddings are computed without leaving our infrastructure. The list of sub-processors is public.

items.q: Which AI models does it use?
items.a: Anthropic's Claude by default, in three tiers: Fast, Standard and Powerful. The router accepts other providers and you can restrict which models are allowed in your organization.

items.q: Is my data used to train models?
items.a: No. Your data is used only to provide the service. Anthropic and AWS Bedrock do not train their models on data received through their API.

items.q: Can I take what I build with me?
items.a: Yes. Every project exports as a runnable .zip or syncs with a GitHub repository. Your agents and workflows run outside Messer.

items.q: How do the trial and billing work?
items.a: You start with 14 days of the Pro plan, no card required. Then you choose a monthly or annual plan; AI usage is deducted from the included credits and you can buy extra packs.
Any tool or step can require human approval. The run pauses, notifies whoever has to decide in the app or by email, and continues once it is approved or denied.

faq.creditA: It is the unit we use to measure AI usage. One credit equals {usd} USD of model usage, and every plan includes an amount of credits each month.
faq.creditAGeneric: It is the unit we use to measure AI usage. Every plan includes an amount of credits each month.
faq.usageA: Every model call records its input and output tokens. We multiply them by the model's public rate, add a {pct}% margin and convert the result into credits. The cost of every run appears in its traces.
faq.usageAGeneric: Every model call records its input and output tokens. We multiply them by the model's public rate, add a margin and convert the result into credits. The cost of every run appears in its traces.
faq.outQ: What happens if I run out of credits?
faq.outA: You can buy a pack at any time or turn on automatic top-up when the balance drops below a threshold. You can also set budgets per organization or per project, with alerts and an automatic hard stop.
faq.changeA: Yes, whenever you want from Plan and billing or from the Stripe customer portal, where you can also download your invoices.
faq.trialA: 14 days of the Pro plan with its features and credits, no card required. When it ends you choose a plan; if you don't, the organization becomes read-only and you keep your projects.
faq.vatA: Yes. Billing is handled by Stripe, which applies the VAT that corresponds to your country and your EU VAT number.
faq.enterpriseA: Strict EU residency, deployment in your cloud or on your servers, SCIM, SLA and a dedicated engineer. Pricing starts at {price} per month and depends on volume.
faq.enterpriseAGeneric: Strict EU residency, deployment in your cloud or on your servers, SCIM, SLA and a dedicated engineer. Pricing depends on volume.

securityPage.metaDescription: Messer trust center: EU data residency, per-organization isolation, encryption, SSO and SCIM, audit, sub-processors and DPA.
securityPage.title: Security, privacy and compliance
securityPage.subtitle: How we protect your company's data and which controls you have over it.

sections.title: EU data residency
sections.body: The database, file storage, job queue, execution services and the website run in European Union regions.
points: Standard mode: Anthropic models through their API, with the rest of the service and your data in the EU.
Strict mode (Enterprise): models are used only through Claude on AWS Bedrock in an EU region and embeddings are computed locally.
In strict mode, voice and email providers must have an EU region or are disabled.

sections.title: Isolation between organizations
sections.body: Every request runs with a database role that cannot bypass security, with Row Level Security on every business table.
points: Policies filter by organization and role in the database itself.
Automated tests check that one organization cannot read anything from another.
Agent and console SQL is read-only, with time and row limits, and restricted to each knowledge base's schema.

sections.title: Encryption
sections.body: Data travels encrypted with TLS and our infrastructure providers store it encrypted at rest.
points: Connector credentials and project secrets are additionally encrypted with a master key (Fernet: AES-128 and HMAC-SHA256).
Passwords with Argon2id; API keys and tokens stored only as hashes.
httpOnly, secure session cookies and a strict content security policy.

sections.title: Identity and access
sections.body: Control who gets in and what each person can do.
points: SSO with SAML 2.0 or OIDC and group-to-role mapping.
User provisioning with SCIM 2.0.
Four roles: owner, admin, builder and viewer.
Two-factor authentication with TOTP and recovery codes.

sections.title: Audit and traceability
sections.body: You know what happened, who did it and what it cost.
points: Insert-only audit log, exportable to CSV.
Full trace of every run: model and tool calls with input, output, tokens, cost and latency.
Configurable retention of traces and conversations per organization.

sections.title: AI controls
sections.body: Agents act within the limits you set.
points: Human approval by default for tools with external effects.
Prompt-injection protection on by default in the Composer, public chats and channels. Documents are treated as data, never as instructions.
Per-organization model policies and budgets with automatic hard stops.
Transparency: public chats tell users they are talking to an AI and the answering model is recorded.

sections.title: Development and operations
sections.body: Security is also about how we build and run the service.
points: Continuous integration with tests, dependency audits (pip-audit and npm audit) and secret scanning.
Automatic backups of the database and storage, with a tested restore.
Error monitoring in the EU and a public status page.

sections.title: Privacy and GDPR
sections.body: We act as the processor of the data you upload to Messer.
points: Data processing agreement (DPA) under Article 28 of the GDPR.
Export and verifiable deletion of the data of a person or a whole organization.
Public list of sub-processors, with advance notice of changes.

securityPage.subprocessorsBody: We work with few providers, all with an EU region except the model providers you choose to use outside strict mode.
